_doc: HMTc Category 21 (Children's Toys, Arts, and Crafts) compiler config. Method v2.0, article form. Every numeric cell names EXPLICIT register ids; the compiler takes the strictest (min) over ids that share a basis. This category is regulated under two fundamentally different bases and the whole config is built to keep them apart. (A) MIGRATION / SOLUBLE: how much element transfers out of accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C stomach-acid extraction. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 splits this into three MATERIAL categories with three different limit sets — Category I dry/brittle/powder-like/pliable, Category II liquid or sticky, Category III scraped-off — and ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) sets soluble-element limits for surface coatings and accessible substrate. (B) TOTAL CONTENT: how much element the material contains — CPSIA s.101 total lead in children's-product substrate and in the dried paint film, Canada SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2018-82/83, RoHS homogeneous-material limits for electrical and electronic equipment, and the REACH Annex XVII cadmium, organotin, Cr(VI)-in-leather and consumer-textile restrictions. EVERY row here publishes on basis (A) and carries basis (B) as a disclosed companion obligation, never as the published number. That direction was chosen because the migration regime spans the whole panel and is the stricter ceiling for lead and cadmium, whereas the content instruments are analyte-narrow and, for cadmium in paint (0.1 percent) and for every RoHS element, dramatically more permissive: publishing a content figure as the HMTc ceiling would replace a protective limit with a permissive one. The one content instrument that is stricter than its migration counterpart — Canada's 10 mg/kg total mercury in surface coating material — is disclosed on every mercury cell as a parallel obligation and surfaces in the audit scan as stricter-unselected, which is the audit working as designed rather than a missed anchor. A per-row basis_guard pins each row to its own EN 71-3 material category plus the ASTM soluble rows, so a Category III value cannot silently anchor a Category I cell and no total-content row can resolve into a migration cell at all. iAs and MeHg are speciation-bounded not-material on every row (no toy instrument speciates arsenic or mercury; there is no methylation pathway in an article). Total chromium is a SCREEN anchored on ASTM F963-17 because the Toy Safety Directive sets Cr(III) and Cr(VI) limits and no total-chromium limit; the health-relevant species Cr(VI) carries its own published cell from the Directive. Antimony, barium and selenium are regulated by the toy-migration instruments but are not HMTc panel analytes; they are screened, not published.

_category.name: Children's Toys, Arts, and Crafts
_category.anchor: EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 element-migration limits, matched per row to the article's real EN 71-3 material category, with ASTM F963-17 soluble-element limits (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) supplying the total-chromium screen; total-content law (CPSIA lead, RoHS, REACH Annex XVII) carried as disclosed companion obligations.
_category.basis_family: Element MIGRATION from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C), expressed in mg/kg of toy material and split by the Directive's three material categories. This is never conflated with total element CONTENT of the material (CPSIA s.101 lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin, the consumer-textile restriction), which is a different measured quantity; content instruments appear only as companion obligations in substantiation and are excluded from every cell by a per-row basis_guard.
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum in the row's native basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; never occurrence-derived). Category 21 publishes on the element-migration basis only, with each row pinned to its own EN 71-3 material category.
_category.method_note: READING THE STRICTER-UNSELECTED FLAGS. The audit scan compares every credible-regulator register row whose product scope matches this category against each cell's binding value, and flags anything stricter that was not named. Three families of flag recur and each has a single standing answer. (1) SIBLING MATERIAL CATEGORIES. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 sets three limit sets for the same instrument, keyed to material form; the Category I and Category II rows share a product scope with Category III, so on a Category III row the Category I and Category II values are always flagged as stricter. They are inapplicable: a limit for dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material, or for liquid or sticky material, does not govern a material that must be scraped to be tested. Each row's basis_guard admits only its own category, so the flagged value could not have been used even if it had been named. (2) ASTM F963-17 NOMINAL ARSENIC, MERCURY AND CHROMIUM. ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07). EN 71-3:2013 and later abolished the correction, so the Directive's figures are compared against the raw result. On a common raw-result footing ASTM's arsenic ceiling is 62.5 mg/kg against the Directive's 47, and its mercury ceiling is 120 mg/kg against the Directive's 94, so the EU value is the stricter limit as enforced and is what HMTc publishes and applies to the raw uncorrected result. Nothing here rests on that convention alone: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so no HMTc cell is looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause. For total chromium, where the Directive sets Cr(III) and Cr(VI) limits and no total-chromium limit, HMTc applies ASTM's nominal 60 mg/kg to the RAW result, which is stricter than ASTM as enforced — deliberate over-compliance, disclosed as such. REGISTER GAPS RECORDED, NOT WORKED AROUND. The EU Cr(III) migration rows of point 13 are absent from the register, as are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg) would be STRICTER than the published total-chromium screen on the Category I and Category II rows, and the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release limit (0.5 ug/cm2/week, a per-area release basis). None is invented into this config; each is returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. (3) CANADIAN TOTAL-MERCURY COATING LIMITS. SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 cap TOTAL mercury at 10 mg/kg in surface coating material. That is a content ceiling, not a migration ceiling; it is a real and binding parallel obligation, it is disclosed on every mercury cell, and it is excluded from the migration cells by the basis_guard because a content limit and a migration limit are different measured quantities. NOT CONVERTED INTO NUMBERS. The US LHAMA regime (15 U.S.C. 1277 / 16 CFR 1500.14(b)(8) via ASTM D-4236) is a chronic-hazard review and labelling duty with no numeric maximum level, and the mechanical requirements of EN 71-1 and ASTM F963-17 (small parts, magnet flux index, projectile kinetic energy, lid supports, balloon and marble warnings) are not metals limits. Neither is converted into a ceiling anywhere in this config.

toys-painted.name: General toys with paint/surface coatings
toys-painted.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-painted.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-painted.scope_note: Toys bearing an accessible applied paint, varnish, lacquer, printing ink, applied sticker, film or other surface coating. The coating itself is the certified material for this row; the toy body underneath is certified under toys-substrate-materials. EN 71-3 clause 9.1 treats coatings of paint, varnish, lacquer, printing ink and polymer as scraped-off material (Category III). Total-lead-in-paint law is the most-cited instrument for painted toys and is carried as a companion CONTENT obligation on every cell, never as the published migration number.
toys-painted.material: Cured surface coating: paint, varnish, lacquer, enamel, printing ink, screen-print, hot-stamp foil, applied decal, sticker and film.
toys-painted.components: Sample each distinct colour and each distinct coating system separately (a multi-colour print is multiple test portions). Scrape the coating to substrate over at least 100 mg per colour without entraining substrate. Sample the coating on any small part or removable accessory separately. Record coating thickness and whether the coating is accessible before and after the use-and-abuse conditioning of ASTM F963-17 8.5 / EN 71-1.
toys-painted.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-painted.basis_guard: element migration from scraped-off toy material \(Category III\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate
toys-painted.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III. The guard admits only the Category III rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so a Category I or Category II value — which belongs to a different material form — cannot silently anchor a cell here, and no total-CONTENT instrument (CPSIA total lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium, the consumer-textile restriction) can be resolved into a migration cell.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken over the EU Toy Safety Directive value and the US ASTM F963-17 soluble-lead value (mandatory under CPSIA s.106).
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (EU Toy Safety Directive value vs ASTM F963-17 soluble cadmium).
Cd.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

tAs.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tAs.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tAs.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-arsenic figure (25 mg/kg, astm_f963_tas_soluble) and the audit scan flags it as stricter-unselected. It is not adopted, and the reason is a comparability defect, not convenience: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the arsenic correction is 60 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2, the table ASTM F963 4.3.5 shares its lineage with). A raw uncorrected result of up to 62.5 mg/kg therefore conforms to ASTM's 25 mg/kg. EN 71-3:2013 and later, which is the method behind the 2009/48/EC figures, abolished the correction, so the Directive's value is compared against the raw result. Expressed on the same raw-result footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling for every material category, and HMTc applies it to the raw uncorrected result. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 and ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in a cured paint, varnish, lacquer, printing-ink or polymer surface coating is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). None of the three speciates arsenic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

tHg.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tHg.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-mercury migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tHg.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-mercury figure (60 mg/kg, astm_f963_thg_soluble), flagged by the audit scan. It is not adopted for the same comparability reason as arsenic: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the mercury correction is 50 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2), so a raw result of up to 120 mg/kg conforms to ASTM's 60 mg/kg, whereas the Directive's figure is compared against the raw result. On the same raw footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause. Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 10 mg/kg TOTAL mercury in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films. That is a total-content ceiling on the coating, a different measured quantity from migration, and it is stricter than the migration ceiling published here. It is carried as a companion obligation rather than substituted into this cell, and HMTc requires conformity with BOTH: an article whose coating carries more than 10 mg/kg total mercury does not certify, whatever its migration result.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. a cured paint, varnish, lacquer, printing-ink or polymer surface coating carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Any organomercury fraction is bounded by the published total-mercury migration ceiling by identity (MeHg <= tHg).
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (mercury, total element); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury (total element); ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (mercury, total element); Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 (total mercury in surface coating material). None speciates mercury.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193), AU-NZ, CODEX, international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

Ni.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here.

Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive tin migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Sn.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling for toy material. The figure is highly permissive and HMTc states it as written rather than inventing a tighter one. Organotin is separately restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-content basis (0.1 percent as tin for DBT and, for skin-contact and childcare articles, DOT); that is a content ceiling on organotin compounds, a different measured quantity, and it is a companion obligation rather than this cell's anchor.

Al.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Al.label: EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/1922).
Al.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric aluminium ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate aluminium. The 2019/1922 amendment already tightened these values by roughly 2.5x; HMTc publishes the amended figures as written.

Cr.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: US ASTM F963-17 soluble total-chromium maximum (mandatory under CPSIA s.106), applied to the raw uncorrected EN 71-3 result.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so ASTM F963-17 is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value in the migration/soluble basis and no strictest-selection over multiple instruments is available. ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07); the chromium correction is 30 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2), so ASTM's enforced raw-result ceiling is about 86 mg/kg. HMTc applies the nominal 60 mg/kg to the RAW uncorrected result, which is stricter than ASTM as enforced. This is deliberate over-compliance in the protective direction and is disclosed rather than presented as the government figure applied on the government's own terms. Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. Neither is invented into this config.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 regulate total chromium only). Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-substrate-materials.name: Toy substrate materials (accessible plastics/metals/woods/rubbers)
toys-substrate-materials.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-substrate-materials.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-substrate-materials.scope_note: The accessible substrate of a toy once any coating is disregarded: moulded and extruded plastics, elastomers and rubbers, wood and wood composites, metals and plated metals, paper and board, glass and ceramic. All are tested by scraping, which is EN 71-3 Category III.
toys-substrate-materials.material: Accessible polymer, elastomer, wood, metal, plated metal, paper/board, glass and ceramic substrate.
toys-substrate-materials.components: One test portion per distinct homogeneous substrate material, taken from accessible surfaces after use-and-abuse conditioning. Plated and painted parts are sampled twice: coating (routed to toys-painted) and substrate beneath. Metal fasteners, rivets, eyelets, springs and magnets are sampled as separate components.
toys-substrate-materials.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-substrate-materials.basis_guard: element migration from scraped-off toy material \(Category III\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate
toys-substrate-materials.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III. The guard admits only the Category III rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so a Category I or Category II value — which belongs to a different material form — cannot silently anchor a cell here, and no total-CONTENT instrument (CPSIA total lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium, the consumer-textile restriction) can be resolved into a migration cell.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken over the EU Toy Safety Directive value and the US ASTM F963-17 soluble-lead value (mandatory under CPSIA s.106).
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.Where the article is a toy intended to come into contact with food (play tea and dinner sets, play food, toy cooking and baking sets), Directive 2009/48/EC additionally requires it to satisfy food-contact law. Regulation (EU) 10/2011 sets specific migration into food far below anything in this row — lead not detectable at 0.01 mg/kg food, cadmium at 0.002, mercury and arsenic at 0.01, total chromium at 0.01, nickel 0.02, aluminium 1 — on a migration-into-food basis that is a third measured quantity. It is a companion obligation for food-contact toys and is never resolved into this cell.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (EU Toy Safety Directive value vs ASTM F963-17 soluble cadmium).
Cd.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

tAs.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tAs.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tAs.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-arsenic figure (25 mg/kg, astm_f963_tas_soluble) and the audit scan flags it as stricter-unselected. toys-stuffing-materials.components: One test portion per distinct fill material and per distinct colour of dyed fill. Sample the fill as supplied inside the finished toy, not the pre-production lot. Where a toy contains a weighting pouch, the pouch fabric routes to toys-stuffed-bean-bag and the weighting medium is tested here.

toys-stuffing-materials.basis_guard_note: This row's defining material form is dry, powder-like or granular fill, which is EN 71-3 Category I. The guard admits only the Category I rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so the looser Category III values cannot anchor a cell here and no total-content instrument can be resolved into a migration cell.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable toy material (EN 71-3 Category I, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category I (dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable) toy material, taken over the EU Toy Safety Directive value and the US ASTM F963-17 soluble-lead value (mandatory under CPSIA s.106).
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 as introduced by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 caps lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) at 1 mg/kg in the homogeneous material of consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles. Fill enclosed inside a toy is neither, so entry 72 is not read across as this row's ceiling; where a fibre fill is also supplied as a loose skin-contact textile, entry 72 binds it directly on a total-content basis and is a companion obligation.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable toy material (EN 71-3 Category I, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category I (dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable) toy material (EU Toy Safety Directive value vs ASTM F963-17 soluble cadmium).
Cd.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

tAs.basis_label: element MIGRATION from dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable toy material (EN 71-3 Category I, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tAs.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-arsenic migration maximum for Category I (dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable) toy material.
tAs.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-arsenic figure (25 mg/kg, astm_f963_tas_soluble) and the audit scan flags it as stricter-unselected. It is not adopted, and the reason is a comparability defect, not convenience: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the arsenic correction is 60 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2, the table ASTM F963 4.3.5 shares its lineage with). A raw uncorrected result of up to 62.5 mg/kg therefore conforms to ASTM's 25 mg/kg. EN 71-3:2013 and later, which is the method behind the 2009/48/EC figures, abolished the correction, so the Directive's value is compared against the raw result. Expressed on the same raw-result footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling for every material category, and HMTc applies it to the raw uncorrected result. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 and ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in loose fill: fibre wadding, foam, granulate, micro-bead, ground shell or bean fill is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). None of the three speciates arsenic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

Cr.basis_label: element MIGRATION from dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable toy material (EN 71-3 Category I, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: US ASTM F963-17 soluble total-chromium maximum (mandatory under CPSIA s.106), applied to the raw uncorrected EN 71-3 result.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so ASTM F963-17 is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value in the migration/soluble basis and no strictest-selection over multiple instruments is available. ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07); the chromium correction is 30 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2), so ASTM's enforced raw-result ceiling is about 86 mg/kg. HMTc applies the nominal 60 mg/kg to the RAW uncorrected result, which is stricter than ASTM as enforced. This is deliberate over-compliance in the protective direction and is disclosed rather than presented as the government figure applied on the government's own terms. Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. Neither is invented into this config.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable toy material (EN 71-3 Category I, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category I (dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable) toy material.
Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 regulate total chromium only). Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-rattles.name: Rattles
toys-rattles.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-rattles.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-rattles.scope_note: Rattles as defined by ASTM F963-17 and EN 71-1: hand-held noise-making toys for infants, including the shell, handle, any teething surface, the internal noise-making pellets and any applied coating. Heavily mouthed by children under 12 months. Teethers and teething toys are certified under HMTc Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products) per the Category 21 boundary rule.
toys-rattles.material: Moulded polymer, wood, metal or textile rattle body; internal pellets or beads; applied coating.
toys-rattles.components: Separate test portions for shell/handle polymer or wood, applied coating (routed to toys-painted), internal pellets or beads, and any elastomer or textile grip. Internal pellets are tested even where they are not accessible in the as-supplied state, because rattle failure is the design hazard the mechanical standards address.
toys-rattles.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-rattles.basis_guard: element migration from scraped-off toy material \(Category III\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate
toys-rattles.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III. The guard admits only the Category III rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so a Category I or Category II value — which belongs to a different material form — cannot silently anchor a cell here, and no total-CONTENT instrument (CPSIA total lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium, the consumer-textile restriction) can be resolved into a migration cell.
toys-rattles.cross_reference: Teething toys and teethers are HMTc Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products), not Category 21. A rattle marketed with a teething surface is certified against both rows.

Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here.

Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive tin migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Sn.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling for toy material. The figure is highly permissive and HMTc states it as written rather than inventing a tighter one. Organotin is separately restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-content basis (0.1 percent as tin for DBT and, for skin-contact and childcare articles, DOT); that is a content ceiling on organotin compounds, a different measured quantity, and it is a companion obligation rather than this cell's anchor.

Al.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Al.label: EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/1922).

Cr.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: US ASTM F963-17 soluble total-chromium maximum (mandatory under CPSIA s.106), applied to the raw uncorrected EN 71-3 result.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so ASTM F963-17 is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value in the migration/soluble basis and no strictest-selection over multiple instruments is available. ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07); the chromium correction is 30 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2), so ASTM's enforced raw-result ceiling is about 86 mg/kg. HMTc applies the nominal 60 mg/kg to the RAW uncorrected result, which is stricter than ASTM as enforced. This is deliberate over-compliance in the protective direction and is disclosed rather than presented as the government figure applied on the government's own terms. Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. Neither is invented into this config.

Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 regulate total chromium only). toys-battery-electronic.name: Battery-operated/electronic toys
toys-battery-electronic.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-battery-electronic.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-battery-electronic.scope_note: Toys containing batteries or electronics: the accessible housing, keypad and button elastomer, display lens, cable and cable sheath, and any accessible plated contact. Inaccessible electrical and electronic material inside the enclosure is NOT accessible toy material and is not reached by EN 71-3; it is governed instead by RoHS on a total-content basis, which is carried as a companion obligation on this row.
toys-battery-electronic.material: Accessible polymer housing, keypad elastomer, display lens, cable sheath, plated contact, applied coating.
toys-battery-electronic.components: Separate test portions for housing polymer (per colour), keypad or button elastomer, display lens, cable sheath, accessible plated contacts and battery-compartment contacts, and applied coating. Battery-compartment security is verified per EN 71-1 / ASTM F963-17 before accessibility is judged. Inaccessible printed-circuit assemblies, solder, wiring and battery cells are assessed against the RoHS companion obligation, not against this row's migration ceilings.
toys-battery-electronic.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-battery-electronic.basis_guard: element migration from scraped-off toy material \(Category III\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate
toys-battery-electronic.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III. The guard admits only the Category III rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so a Category I or Category II value — which belongs to a different material form — cannot silently anchor a cell here, and no total-CONTENT instrument (CPSIA total lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium, the consumer-textile restriction) can be resolved into a migration cell. Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS) caps lead, mercury and Cr(VI) at 0.1 percent and cadmium at 0.01 percent by weight in each HOMOGENEOUS MATERIAL of electrical and electronic equipment. That is a total-content ceiling on a different measured quantity, it is far more permissive than the migration ceilings published here, and admitting it into a migration cell would replace a protective limit with a permissive one. It is therefore excluded by the guard and disclosed as a parallel obligation on the inaccessible EEE materials that migration testing never reaches.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken over the EU Toy Safety Directive value and the US ASTM F963-17 soluble-lead value (mandatory under CPSIA s.106).
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number. Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS) additionally caps lead at 0.1 percent by weight in each homogeneous EEE material (eu_rohs_2011_pb_homogeneous_materials_1000000). It is a total-content ceiling, roughly 43x more permissive than the migration ceiling published here, and it reaches material that EN 71-3 does not; HMTc requires conformity with both and never substitutes one for the other.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (EU Toy Safety Directive value vs ASTM F963-17 soluble cadmium).
Cd.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit. RoHS additionally caps cadmium at 0.01 percent by weight in each homogeneous EEE material (eu_rohs_2011_cd_homogeneous_materials_100000), again on a total-content basis and as a parallel obligation.

tAs.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tAs.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tAs.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-arsenic figure (25 mg/kg, astm_f963_tas_soluble) and the audit scan flags it as stricter-unselected. It is not adopted, and the reason is a comparability defect, not convenience: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the arsenic correction is 60 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2, the table ASTM F963 4.3.5 shares its lineage with). A raw uncorrected result of up to 62.5 mg/kg therefore conforms to ASTM's 25 mg/kg. EN 71-3:2013 and later, which is the method behind the 2009/48/EC figures, abolished the correction, so the Directive's value is compared against the raw result. Expressed on the same raw-result footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling for every material category, and HMTc applies it to the raw uncorrected result. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 and ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in an accessible housing, keypad, lens, cable sheath or plated contact is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). None of the three speciates arsenic.

On the same raw footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause. Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 10 mg/kg TOTAL mercury in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films. That is a total-content ceiling on the coating, a different measured quantity from migration, and it is stricter than the migration ceiling published here. It is carried as a companion obligation rather than substituted into this cell, and HMTc requires conformity with BOTH: an article whose coating carries more than 10 mg/kg total mercury does not certify, whatever its migration result. RoHS additionally caps mercury at 0.1 percent by weight in each homogeneous EEE material (eu_rohs_2011_thg_homogeneous_materials_1000000), relevant to backlight and lamp components. Total-content basis, parallel obligation.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. an accessible housing, keypad, lens, cable sheath or plated contact carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Any organomercury fraction is bounded by the published total-mercury migration ceiling by identity (MeHg <= tHg).
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (mercury, total element); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury (total element); ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (mercury, total element); Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 (total mercury in surface coating material). None speciates mercury.

tHg.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

On the same raw footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause. Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 10 mg/kg TOTAL mercury in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films. Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: US ASTM F963-17 soluble total-chromium maximum (mandatory under CPSIA s.106), applied to the raw uncorrected EN 71-3 result.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so ASTM F963-17 is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value in the migration/soluble basis and no strictest-selection over multiple instruments is available. Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. toys-with-magnets.scope_note: Toys containing magnets or magnetic components: magnetic construction sets, magnetic figures and tiles, magnetic drawing boards, fridge-magnet craft toys and magnetic fishing games. toys-with-magnets.basis_guard: element migration from scraped-off toy material \(Category III\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate

toys-balls.material: Rubber, foam, PVC/vinyl, polymer shell, textile cover, bladder, printed decoration.
toys-balls.components: Separate test portions for ball wall or shell (per colour), foam core, textile cover and its stitching, internal bladder, valve, and printed or screen-printed decoration.
toys-balls.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-balls.basis_guard: element migration from scraped-off toy material \(Category III\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate
toys-balls.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III. The guard admits only the Category III rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so a Category I or Category II value — which belongs to a different material form — cannot silently anchor a cell here, and no total-CONTENT instrument (CPSIA total lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium, the consumer-textile restriction) can be resolved into a migration cell.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken over the EU Toy Safety Directive value and the US ASTM F963-17 soluble-lead value (mandatory under CPSIA s.106).
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (EU Toy Safety Directive value vs ASTM F963-17 soluble cadmium).
Cd.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

tAs.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tAs.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tAs.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-arsenic figure (25 mg/kg, astm_f963_tas_soluble) and the audit scan flags it as stricter-unselected. It is not adopted, and the reason is a comparability defect, not convenience: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the arsenic correction is 60 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2, the table ASTM F963 4.3.5 shares its lineage with). A raw uncorrected result of up to 62.5 mg/kg therefore conforms to ASTM's 25 mg/kg. EN 71-3:2013 and later, which is the method behind the 2009/48/EC figures, abolished the correction, so the Directive's value is compared against the raw result. Expressed on the same raw-result footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling for every material category, and HMTc applies it to the raw uncorrected result. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 and ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in a rubber, foam, plastic or textile ball wall and its printing is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). None of the three speciates arsenic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

None speciates mercury.

Ni.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all. Al.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Al.label: EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/1922).

Cr.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: US ASTM F963-17 soluble total-chromium maximum (mandatory under CPSIA s.106), applied to the raw uncorrected EN 71-3 result.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so ASTM F963-17 is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value in the migration/soluble basis and no strictest-selection over multiple instruments is available. ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07); the chromium correction is 30 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2), so ASTM's enforced raw-result ceiling is about 86 mg/kg. HMTc applies the nominal 60 mg/kg to the RAW uncorrected result, which is stricter than ASTM as enforced. This is deliberate over-compliance in the protective direction and is disclosed rather than presented as the government figure applied on the government's own terms. Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. Neither is invented into this config.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 regulate total chromium only). Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-marbles.name: Marbles
toys-marbles.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-marbles.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-marbles.scope_note: Marbles and marble-like play spheres in glass, glazed ceramic, stone or polymer, including marbles supplied inside games and runs. Glass and ceramic are tested by scraping/grinding, which is EN 71-3 Category III. toys-marbles.components: Separate test portions for glass body, internal colour cane or vane (the pigmented phase, which is where metals concentrate in glass marbles), ceramic body, ceramic glaze, and any applied surface coating or metallic lustre.

The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.

Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

tAs.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tAs.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tAs.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-arsenic figure (25 mg/kg, astm_f963_tas_soluble) and the audit scan flags it as stricter-unselected. It is not adopted, and the reason is a comparability defect, not convenience: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the arsenic correction is 60 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2, the table ASTM F963 4.3.5 shares its lineage with). A raw uncorrected result of up to 62.5 mg/kg therefore conforms to ASTM's 25 mg/kg. EN 71-3:2013 and later, which is the method behind the 2009/48/EC figures, abolished the correction, so the Directive's value is compared against the raw result. Expressed on the same raw-result footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling for every material category, and HMTc applies it to the raw uncorrected result. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 and ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in a mobile, activity-panel or attached-toy surface within infant reach is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.

not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
