tHg.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tHg.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-mercury migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tHg.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-mercury figure (60 mg/kg, astm_f963_thg_soluble), flagged by the audit scan. It is not adopted for the same comparability reason as arsenic: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the mercury correction is 50 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2), so a raw result of up to 120 mg/kg conforms to ASTM's 60 mg/kg, whereas the Directive's figure is compared against the raw result. On the same raw footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause. Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 10 mg/kg TOTAL mercury in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films. That is a total-content ceiling on the coating, a different measured quantity from migration, and it is stricter than the migration ceiling published here. It is carried as a companion obligation rather than substituted into this cell, and HMTc requires conformity with BOTH: an article whose coating carries more than 10 mg/kg total mercury does not certify, whatever its migration result.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. a stroller-, carriage- or car-seat-attached toy surface carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Any organomercury fraction is bounded by the published total-mercury migration ceiling by identity (MeHg <= tHg).
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (mercury, total element); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury (total element); ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (mercury, total element); Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 (total mercury in surface coating material). None speciates mercury.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193), AU-NZ, CODEX, international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

Cr.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: US ASTM F963-17 soluble total-chromium maximum (mandatory under CPSIA s.106), applied to the raw uncorrected EN 71-3 result.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so ASTM F963-17 is the only credible sovereign total-chromium value in the migration/soluble basis and no strictest-selection over multiple instruments is available. ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07); the chromium correction is 30 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2), so ASTM's enforced raw-result ceiling is about 86 mg/kg. HMTc applies the nominal 60 mg/kg to the RAW uncorrected result, which is stricter than ASTM as enforced. This is deliberate over-compliance in the protective direction and is disclosed rather than presented as the government figure applied on the government's own terms. Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. Neither is invented into this config.

Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.

toy-chests.name: Toy chests
toy-chests.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toy-chests.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toy-chests.scope_note: Toy chests, toy boxes and lidded toy storage supplied for children's use, including the body material, the lid and its finish, hinges and lid supports, and any applied decal. Lid-support and ventilation requirements under EN 71-1 and ASTM F963-17 4.41 are mechanical and are not converted into a metals number. The chest's applied finish is also certified under toys-painted, where the total-lead-in-paint content obligation is recorded; that content rule names furniture articles expressly (CPSIA s.101 / 16 CFR 1303) and is a companion obligation here, not this row's ceiling.
toy-chests.material: Solid wood, plywood, MDF/particleboard, moulded plastic or sheet metal body; applied lacquer or paint; hinge, lid support, handle and caster.
toy-chests.components: Separate test portions for body material (wood, composite, plastic or metal), applied finish per colour (routed to toys-painted), applied decal or transfer, hinge and lid-support metal, handle, caster, and any textile or foam lining. Sample the interior surfaces as well as the exterior: a child sits inside a toy chest.
toy-chests.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toy-chests.basis_guard: element migration from scraped-off toy material \(Category III\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate
toy-chests.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III. The guard admits only the Category III rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so a Category I or Category II value — which belongs to a different material form — cannot silently anchor a cell here, and no total-CONTENT instrument (CPSIA total lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium, the consumer-textile restriction) can be resolved into a migration cell.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken over the EU Toy Safety Directive value and the US ASTM F963-17 soluble-lead value (mandatory under CPSIA s.106).
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (EU Toy Safety Directive value vs ASTM F963-17 soluble cadmium).
Cd.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

tAs.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
tAs.label: EU Toy Safety Directive total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
tAs.substantiation: ASTM F963-17 carries a nominally lower soluble-arsenic figure (25 mg/kg, astm_f963_tas_soluble) and the audit scan flags it as stricter-unselected. It is not adopted, and the reason is a comparability defect, not convenience: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 states its soluble-element limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an ADJUSTED result: a per-element analytical correction is subtracted from the laboratory result before comparison to the limit (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2 — 60 percent arsenic, 50 percent mercury, 30 percent chromium, lead and cadmium — ingested at wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, which records that F963 4.3.5 sits in that lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07), and the arsenic correction is 60 percent (ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 2, the table ASTM F963 4.3.5 shares its lineage with). A raw uncorrected result of up to 62.5 mg/kg therefore conforms to ASTM's 25 mg/kg. EN 71-3:2013 and later, which is the method behind the 2009/48/EC figures, abolished the correction, so the Directive's value is compared against the raw result. Expressed on the same raw-result footing the EU value is the stricter enforced ceiling for every material category, and HMTc applies it to the raw uncorrected result. The comparison is not left to rest on that convention, however: HMTc requires conformity with the ASTM figure on ASTM's own corrected-result terms as a companion obligation IN ADDITION to the raw-result ceiling published here, so the HMTc cell is not looser than ASTM under either reading of the correction clause.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 and ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in a wood, wood-composite, plastic or metal chest surface and its finish is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.

None of the three speciates arsenic.

art-craft-materials.name: Art & craft materials (paints, markers, crayons, colored pencils, inks, adhesives/glues, modeling clay, putties/gels/slimes, glitter/pigments, jewelry/craft kits)
art-craft-materials.native_basis: element migration from liquid or sticky toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category II; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
art-craft-materials.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from liquid or sticky toy material (EN 71-3 Category II, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
art-craft-materials.scope_note: Children's art and craft materials. The row's scope spans all three EN 71-3 material categories at once: liquid and sticky materials (poster and tempera paint, finger paint, liquid ink and marker fluid, glue and adhesive, slime, putty and gel) are Category II; dry, brittle and pliable materials (crayons, chalk, pastel and pencil cores, powder pigment, glitter, modelling clay and dough) are Category I; and finished craft-kit components (beads, jewellery findings, wire, cord, plastic and wooden parts) are Category III. Category II carries the strictest of the three limit sets for every panel analyte, and Directive 2009/48/EC applies it to material that is unambiguously within this row's scope, so Category II is the published ceiling for the whole row. That is the strictest-applicable selection required by Method v2.0 step 3 within a single instrument; it is not a blend, and applying it to the row's Category I and Category III components is deliberate over-compliance, disclosed here rather than presented as those components' own legal ceiling.
art-craft-materials.material: Liquid and sticky: poster/tempera/finger paint, ink, marker fluid, glue, slime, putty, gel. Dry and pliable: crayon, chalk, pastel, pencil core, powder pigment, glitter, modelling clay and dough. Finished components: beads, findings, wire, cord.
art-craft-materials.components: Separate test portions per colour and per material form. Liquid and sticky materials are sampled as supplied without drying. Crayons, pastels and pencil cores are sampled as the pigmented core with the wooden casing and lacquer tested separately. Powder pigment and glitter are sampled undiluted. Modelling compounds are sampled per colour. Jewellery and craft-kit components are itemised: metal beads and findings, plated parts, glass and acrylic beads, cord and elastic, and any supplied tool.
art-craft-materials.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
art-craft-materials.basis_guard: element migration from liquid or sticky toy material \(Category II\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from surface coating or accessible substrate
art-craft-materials.basis_guard_note: This row's scope contains liquid and sticky materials, which is EN 71-3 Category II and carries the strictest of the three category limit sets. The guard admits only the Category II rows of Directive 2009/48/EC and the ASTM F963-17 soluble rows, so a Category I or Category III value cannot anchor a cell here and no total-content instrument can be resolved into a migration cell. The US LHAMA regime (15 U.S.C. 1277 / 16 CFR 1500.14(b)(8), implemented through ASTM D-4236) imposes a chronic-hazard review by a qualified toxicologist and a labelling duty on art materials. It sets NO numeric maximum level for any element. A labelling and review duty is not convertible into a ceiling and none is derived from it here; LHAMA conformity is recorded as a separate documentary requirement.

This is deliberate over-compliance in the protective direction and is disclosed rather than presented as the government figure applied on the government's own terms. Two register gaps are recorded against this cell rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register, and so are the ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 material-category tiers, whose modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits (25 mg/kg each) are STRICTER than the value published here and would bind the Category I and Category II rows if ingested. Neither is invented into this config.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from liquid or sticky toy material (EN 71-3 Category II, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category II (liquid or sticky) toy material.
Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 regulate total chromium only). Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.
